newsitem.title: USA: BMC West Q2 hurt by weather, fewer permits.
newsitem.headline: BMC West Q2 hurt by weather, fewer permits.

text.p: BMC West Corp, a distributor of building materials in the western United States, reported lower second quarter sales and earnings citing unusual weather Texas and lower building permit activity in the majority of its 10-state market area as contributing to the decline.

"Summer is traditionally a strong period for residential construction," the company added. "We are optimistic about the long-term job growth in our market area and other strong economic indicators that influence housing growth."

Sales for the second quarter were off one percent to $190.6 million. Net income of $3.5 million was virtually flat with the comparable 1996 quarter which included a $342,000 write-off of unamortized loan costs. Earnings per share were $0.29, down from $0.35, after the $0.03 effect of the write-off, a year ago. Earnings per share were affected by 18 percent more shares outstanding.
"Sales were hurt by a combination of a decline in the number of new building permits and unusually inclement weather conditions," said Donald Hendrickson, chief executive officer.
"Independently, each one of these factors affects the demand for building materials and this year the impact was intensified by both occurring together."
Building permits in BMC West's 10-state market area for the quarter were behind the previous year by 14 percent. Prices for commodity wood and other products were flat with a year ago.

"Despite the substantial decrease in building permit activity, same-store sales decreased only 3 percent," said Hendrickson. "In addition, we are pleased with the positive same-store sales results at 24 of our building materials centers.
"Extreme weather conditions in Texas negatively affected construction activity and our same-store sales in Texas were down significantly during the quarter," he said.
"Our 11 units in Texas account for approximately 25 percent of total sales."
